chunks: And said the Seal of the Hadith Scholars, Sheikh al-Nuri, in the Conclusion of al-Mustadrak:

'The Sheikh of the great Sheikhs and the Proof of the noble guiding Proofs, the Reviver of the Sharia and the Obliterator of vile Innovation, the Inspired one of Truth and its Guide, the Beacon of Religion and its Path, the possessor of the well-known Mahdawi tawqi'at upon which the consensus of the Imamiyya has been transmitted, and the one exclusively distinguished by the distinctions and sublime virtues therein, and besides these the manifest karamat, lofty spiritual stations, and numerous, dazzling, and splendid disputations...'

key_terms.إِجْمَاعُ الْإِمَامِيَّةِ: consensus of the Imamiyya — unanimous agreement of Twelver Shia scholars
key_terms.التَّوْقِيعَاتِ الْمَهْدَوِيَّةِ: Mahdawi tawqi'at — signed letters and responses attributed to Imam al-Mahdi (AS) during his occultation
key_terms.الْكَرَامَاتِ الْجَلِيَّةِ: manifest karamat — divinely bestowed miraculous gifts evident to all observers
key_terms.خَاتِمَةُ الْمُحَدِّثِينَ: Seal of the Hadith Scholars — honorific title of Sheikh al-Nuri, signifying the last of the great hadith transmitters

ai.seo_question: What titles and qualities did Sheikh al-Nuri ascribe to the praised scholar in the conclusion of Mustadrak al-Wasa'il?
ai.summary: This passage is a laudatory biographical encomium by Mirza Husayn Nuri (the Seal of the Hadith Scholars), excerpted from the conclusion of his Mustadrak al-Wasa'il, bestowing the most exalted epithets upon a supreme Shia scholar — most likely Sheikh al-Mufid (d. 413 AH), the renowned recipient of tawqi'at signed by Imam al-Mahdi (AS). The praised figure is described as the reviver of the Sharia, obliterator of vile innovation, possessor of the Mahdawi tawqi'at attested by Imami consensus, holder of manifest karamat, lofty spiritual stations, and brilliant theological disputations.
